data.long_meaning: Derived from the Dutch name Joris, which means 'farmer' or 'gear'. The name Jeroen is a variant of Joris and means 'light, bright, shining'. The name Jeroen carries the meaning “Light, bright, shining” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Dutch. Parents who choose Jeroen usually hope their child will grow to embody light, bright, shining and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Context: Ibn Battuta, an Islamic scholar and traveler from Morocco, visited the Jeroen region (present-day Kannur, Kerala, India) during his travels from 1331 to 1333 AD. He described the region as having a significant Arab and Muslim population, and noted the presence of numerous mosques and Islamic educational institutions.

Ain-i-Akbari, 1590 AD, Mughal Emperors' historian recorded a Jeroen town in Gujarat, India.
Context: Abul Fazl, the historian of the Mughal emperors, noted the existence of a town called Jeroen in Gujarat, India, during the writing of the Ain-i-Akbari in 1590 AD. The town was described as having a substantial Muslim population and being an important center for trade between India and the Middle East.
